en: The Ritual Procedure for the Daily Offering.
Oṃ, homage to Śrī Vajrasattva!
Now begins the ritual procedure for the daily offering.

Therein, first, having performed the ritual rinsing (ācamana) three times with the mantra: "Oṃ hrīṃ svāhā, svāhā to the purification of the body," one should perform the formal resolve (saṃkalpa) regarding the articles of worship.
That is as follows: after the recitation of the resolve beginning with "Oṃ today, O glorious Śrī... and so forth, one should recite this mantra.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Puṣpaketurāja.
It is as follows: Oṃ puṣpe puṣpe, mahāpuṣpe, supuṣpe, puṣpodbhave, puṣpasaṃbhave, puṣpāvakiraṇe, svāhā!
I now offer this golden vessel of flowers, accompanied by flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, flavors, food offerings, and so forth.
Then, having performed the breath-control (prāṇāyāma) and other rites, as well as the ritual placement (nyāsa) and yoga, and having paid homage to the Guru, one should worship the conch.
Oṃ, homage to the gurus, thrice. The command of all the gurus:
Oṃ ā hūṃ vaṃ, vajrodake hūṃ svāhā!
One should sprinkle water from a conch upon the head, saying:
"Just as all the Tathāgatas were bathed immediately upon their birth,
so shall I bathe you with pure, divine water."
Oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamaśriye hūṃ.
Again,

having sipped water with the mantra *oṃ hrīḥ svāhā*, and having consecrated the articles of worship with the previously mentioned mantra, one should place a single flower upon the ground after performing the consecration of the three bodies (*trikāya*).
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ 3 tiṣṭha vajrāsane hūṃ.
[Reciting this,] one should cast two flowers from both sides.
Oṃ sarvapāpānapanaya hūṃ.
One should place one [mark] on the head with this mantra: *oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca huṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā*.
Having made a tilaka on the maṇḍala, one should adorn oneself:
*oṃ vajratilakabhūṣaṇe svāhā*.
One should pour water, flowers, unbroken rice, and incense onto the maṇḍala with this mantra: oṃ vajrodake hūṃ / oṃ vajragomaye hūṃ /
Oṃ, on the vajra-ground with its excellent lines, may all the Tathāgatas bestow their empowerment; svāhā!
One should recite this.
Generosity consists of cow-dung and water, and ethical discipline consists of sweeping clean.
Patience is the removal of tiny ants; vigor is the application of effort;
meditation is making the mind one-pointed at that very moment; and wisdom is the blazing of a flawless line—these six perfections alone one obtains by constructing the maṇḍala of the Sage.
He becomes golden-hued, liberated from all diseases, distinguished among gods and men, with a radiant splendor like the moon;
he is born into a royal lineage, enriched with wealth and gold.
Having performed bodily actions within this supreme abode of the Sugata,
Oṃ sulekhe, may all the Tathāgatas empower this! Svāhā!
Placing a single flower upon the hand, making the hand face downward, one should cast it into the maṇḍala.
Oṃ candrārkavimale, svāhā!

Having circumambulated the maṇḍala clockwise, one should cast a single flower into the vessel for the offering. Reciting "Oṃ Vajrasattva, dispel all obstacles! Hūṃ," and having performed two circumambulations in the sequence starting from the east, one should perform the scattering of twenty-one flowers within the maṇḍala.
Oṃ haḥ, homage to Meru in the great center.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Meru in the middle. Oṃ sūṃ, homage to Meru in the subtle center.
Thus in the center:
Oṃ yaṃ, homage to Pūrvavideha; Pū. Oṃ raṃ, homage to Jambūdvīpa; Da.
Oṃ laṃ, homage to Aparagodānīya; pa. Oṃ vaṃ, homage to Uttarakuru; u.
Oṃ yā, homage to Upadvīpa; a.
Oṃ rā, homage to the subcontinent; nai. Oṃ lā, homage to the subcontinent; vā.
Oṃ vā, homage to Upadvīpa;
ī, likewise;
īṃ yaḥ, homage to the elephant-treasure (gajaratna).
Īṃ raḥ, homage to the jewel of the horse.
Oṃ laḥ, homage to the jewel of the person. Oṃ vaḥ, homage to the jewel of the woman.
Oṃ yā, homage to the sword-jewel!
Oṃ rā, homage to the wheel-jewel! Oṃ lā, homage to the gem-jewel!
Oṃ vā, homage to all treasures! Ī!
Oṃ caṃ, homage to the Moon! Da!
Oṃ sūṃ, homage to the Sun! U!
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ. Homage to the Guru, the glorious Vajrasattva. [In the center:
The fivefold offering.
Oṃ vajragandhe svāhā / Incense. Oṃ vajrapuṣpe svāhā / Flowers.
Flower: Oṃ vajradhūpe svāhā. Incense: [Oṃ vajradhūpe svāhā].
Oṃ vajranaivedye svāhā / the food offering; oṃ vajradīpe svāhā / the lamp offering.
The lamp: Oṃ vajralājāya svāhā. The parched grain: lājāṃ.
One should pour a stream of water mixed with flowers and unbroken rice-grains (*akṣata*) upon the mandala, reciting:
*Oṃ! [This is] Meru, consisting of the four jewels, adorned with the eight continents, strewn with various gems; may it grant that which is unsurpassed.*
To the gurus, to the Buddha and the Dharma, and likewise to the Saṅgha,
I offer with my whole being this complete maṇḍala of jewels.
Praise: Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ!

Homage to the lotus feet of the glorious Vajrasattva, the supreme Guru, who brings forth the illumination of perfect wisdom! Haṃ, homage to you; homage, homage to you! O Lord Guru, I bow to you with devotion;
be gracious to me!
One should stand with palms joined in reverence to him,
by whose rays of grace the darkness is destroyed through the surrounding radiance of the jewel of the true nature of the self, which has been made to shimmer.
Beholding him with clear vision and with playful grace, this salutation is offered to that Guru-Bhāskara.
Homage to the Buddha, the Teacher; homage to the Dharma, the Protector;
homage to the great Saṅgha—homage always to all three.
I pay homage to all the Buddhas and to the Dharma spoken by the Victors;
and to the Saṅgha endowed with moral discipline—to you, the Three Jewels, let there be homage.
I take refuge in the Three Jewels; I confess all my misdeeds;
I rejoice in the merits of the world; and I direct my mind toward the enlightenment of a Buddha.
Until enlightenment, I go for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the supreme Assembly;
I generate the mind of awakening for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of myself and others.
I generate the supreme mind of awakening; I invite all sentient beings.
I shall practice the desired, excellent conduct of awakening so that I may become a Buddha for the benefit of the world.
I shall confess all my misdeeds, rejoice in all merits,
and, having observed the fast, practice the noble eightfold Upoṣadha.
Whatever evil has come upon me through my youth and delusion— whether it be naturally reprehensible, reprehensible by convention, or indeed reprehensible in every respect— [I confess it].
Standing before the Protectors with palms joined, terrified by suffering, I confess that transgression while prostrating again and again.
May the Leaders accept each transgression as a transgression;
this was not good, and it shall not be done by me again.

Just as those Tathāgatas, noble Arhats, perfectly enlightened Buddhas, know and see with their Buddha-knowledge and Buddha-eye that root of merit— its kind, its category, its nature, its essence, its characteristics,
and how it exists according to the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā).

I dedicate that root of merit constantly toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; in this way I dedicate it, so that by means of this, at the same time as my own, there may always be the power to remove the suffering of the world and to bring about its happiness, just as the sun [possesses the power] to dispel darkness and produce light.

Whether seen, heard, or come to mind, or having entered into various discourses and applications, may I act in every way for the benefit of the world, incessantly for its connection with happiness. Thus.
At this juncture, one should perform the *jāpayoga*.

At its conclusion, one should offer a handful of conch-water into the vessel for the offering to Amṛtakuṇḍalin with this: *oṃ hrīṃ ācamanaṃ [prokṣaṇaṃ] praticcha svāhā*. This is the visualization (*bhāvanā*).
Then, by means of the syllable *yaṃ*, a wind mandala is produced; by the syllable *raṃ*, a fire mandala; above that, upon a crest made of three skulls, a white lotus vessel;

therein, it is filled with food and so forth. Above that, having produced the forms of the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and the five lamps (*pañcapradīpa*) arising from the syllables *bruṃ*, *āṃ*, *jiṃ*, *khaṃ*, *huṃ*, *lāṃ*, *māṃ*, *pāṃ*, and *tāṃ*, one should then display the Garuḍa mudrā.
PHREṂ 3.
Again, one should offer a handful of conch-water with this: OṂ INDRĀDILOKAPĀLEBHYAḤ PĀDYĀCAMANAṂ [NĀRṢAṂ] PROKṢAṆAṂ PRATICCHA SVĀHĀ.

Having displayed the mudrās JAḤ HUṂ VAṂ HOḤ, and having displayed the mudrās of the ten world-protectors beginning with Indra, one should cast flowers into the offering vessel in the sequence starting from the east with these mantras.
Oṃ, svāhā to Indra!
Oṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa! Oṃ, svāhā to Kuvera!
Oṃ, to Agni, svāhā! Oṃ, to Nairṛti, svāhā! Oṃ, to Vāyu, svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to Īśāna! Oṃ, svāhā to Brahmā above! Oṃ, svāhā to the earths below!
Oṃ, to Sūrya, the lord of the planets, svāhā! Oṃ, to Candra and the others, the lords of the lunar mansions, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the nāgas, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the asuras, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the yakṣas, svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to the world-protectors of all the cardinal and intermediate directions!
The fivefold offering (*pañcopacāra-pūjā*) and the praise are as before:
"The great heroes beginning with Indra, the world-protectors of great supernatural power..."
May the ten wrathful deities pin you down; O remover of obstacles, homage be to you!
The libation (*tarpaṇa*):

[One should visualize] Mañjughoṣa, whose body is slender and whose head bears the beautiful form of Maitreya, who holds the image of a Buddha like a mass of suns and possesses the mark of a drop (*bindu*).

Having prostrated before the fivefold form—the one seated upon a lotus, whose body is like a staff, the wielder of the thunderbolt with a most excellent form, possessing a terrifying roar, consciousness itself in the form of primordial wisdom, who has cast away the fear of cyclic existence; I pay homage.
One should cause a stream of water with fresh flowers to fall into the vessel for the offering:
"May Indra and the others, together with the hosts of gods and the Vajra-holders, accept this distinguished offering!
[So too may] Agni, Yama, Nairṛti, the Lord of Beings (Bhūpati), the Lord of Waters (Apāmpati), Vāyu, and the Lord of Wealth (Dhanādhipa)."
Īśāna, the lord of beings, and the gods; those above, including the Moon, the Sun, and the Grandfather (Brahmā);
all the gods on earth and the nāgas; the mountains together with the hosts of secret ones (guhyakas).
Let each and every being in their respective directions announce themselves;
may you, being pleased, accept [this offering] together with your retinues, along with your sons, wives, and hosts of servants.
May they, joyful and serene, accept, enjoy, and drink this garland, perfume, flower, offering, incense, and ointment; and may this rite of mine become fruitful.

Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā! Again, likewise: Oṃ! Homage to the Triple Gem! Oṃ to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi, the Great Wrathful One, whose fangs are fierce and terrifying, who holds a sword, a mace, and a noose in his hands! Oṃ Amṛtakuṇḍali! Kha kha khāhi khāhi! Tiṣṭha tiṣṭha! Bandha bandha! Hana hana! Daha daha! Paca pacā! Garjaya garjaya! Tarjaya tarjaya! Visphoṭaya visphoṭaya! To Mahāgaṇapati, the Ender of Life! Hūṃ!
HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.

Therein is the worship with flowers and so forth. Regarding its ritual procedure: at the conclusion of the lamp offering during the worship of the deity, one should worship with parched grains (lājā) while reciting this verse.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has explained their cause, as well as their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
One should worship with flowers, unbroken rice grains, and water with this [mantra]:
*Oṃ, the syllable A is the mouth of all phenomena because they are primordially unarisen;
Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā.*
The sacrificial fee:
Oṃ, to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Greatly Compassionate One, I offer this gift of rice; may I be satisfied.
One should stand with hands joined in the *añjali* gesture,
[reciting]: *Oṃ vajrasattvasamayam anupālaya vajrasattvatvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava sutoṣyo me bhava supoṣyo me bhava anurakto me bhava sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha sarvakarmasu ca*.
"Make my mind glorious, hūṃ ha ha ha ha ho! O Blessed One, [Embodiment of] All Tathāgatas, do not abandon me; become a vajra, O Great Samaya-being, āḥ!
Thus concludes the ritual of the Guru-maṇḍala.
Then, for the purpose of worshipping the deity, one should place a flower upon the head of the deity and recite this meditative formula:
*oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśuddho ’ham* / *oṃ śūnyatājñānavajrasvabhāvātmako ’ham*.
The incense mantra:
Oṃ, Blessed One, Śrī [Name] Vajra-vidyārāja, homage be to you!
O Protector whose nature is compassion, I desire to perform the maṇḍala for you.
Out of compassion for the disciples and for your own worship.
Therefore, O Blessed One, you should show favor to me, your devotee;
may the Buddhas, who bestow the purpose of the wheel of activity for the world, attend to me.
Bodhisattvas established in the fruit, as well as other mantra-deities, deities and world-protectors, and spirits accomplished through perfect awakening.
O you who possess the vajra-eye, whatever beings there may be who delight in the teaching, out of compassion for me and my disciples, [act] toward them.
"I shall worship the preceptor named [Amukadevatā].
Therein I offer Vajra-incense; therein accept the Vajra-incense, svāhā!
Then, holding a handful of flowers directly before him, one should recite this verse of supplication:
Today my birth has become fruitful, and my life as well;
I have undoubtedly realized the commitment of all the gods.
With a mind solely intent on the thought of awakening, I shall become irreversible;
today, my birth in the family of the Tathāgatas will come to pass, without a doubt.
Today is indeed my auspicious day; today is my unsurpassed sacrifice.
Today is indeed the assembly and the manifestation of existence, because of the invitation to all the Buddhas.
Reciting the mantra "Oṃ kusumāñjalinātha hoḥ," one should scatter [the flowers] in the presence of the deity.
Following that is the ritual for bathing.

Therein, first, having placed a bright, clear, and stainless bronze mirror upon a vessel made of gold or other precious materials, and having inscribed a single *praṇava* (oṃ) upon it with a golden stylus, one should pour a stream of water over it while reciting this verse:
"Oṃ! Whatever auspiciousness resides in the hearts of all sentient beings..."
May that supreme consecration be your auspiciousness— the great bliss which is the sovereign of the excellent Dharma family, which is the self of all, and which is entirely free from every defect.
Again, one should bathe [the image] with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) with:
*oṃ sarvatathāgata bruṃ āṃ jiṃ huṃ*. Then, one should show the reflection [of the deity] with this [mantra].
Phenomena are like reflections: transparent, pure, and unclouded;
they are ungraspable and untainted, arising from causes and karma.
One should sprinkle the bathing water upon the region of one's own head with the mantra:
*oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaṃ samāśriye hūṃ*. At the conclusion of the bathing rite, one should draw a circle with a stream of water near the deity.
Oṃ, on the vajra-ground with excellent lines, may all the Tathāgatas bestow their empowerment; svāhā!
Oṃ, vajra-golden stream of water, svāhā!
One should adorn it with vermilion.
I give you this supreme, pure fragrance, which is most excellent for the sense of smell; accept it with supreme devotion as you please. Oṃ vajragandhe svāhā.
Oṃ vajratilakabhūṣaṇe svāhā. [The sacred thread.
Oṃ vajravastrālaṅkārapūjāmeghasamudrasphuraṇayajñopavīta vajrabodhyaṅga dṛḍhakavaca vajravastraṃ svāhā.
Then, having consecrated a flower one hundred and eight times with the root mantra of the deity, one should offer that flower to the deities [upon the head of the deity], saying:
"May the Buddhas grant you well-being; may the gods, together with the Śakras, grant you well-being."
May all beings grant you well-being at all times.
By the power of the Buddha’s merit and through the intention of the deities,
may every purpose that is desired be fully accomplished this very day.
May there be well-being for you bipeds; may there be well-being for you quadrupeds.
May there be well-being for you as you travel on the road, and well-being when you have returned.
May there be well-being at night, may there be well-being by day, and may there be well-being when the sun stands at midday;
may there be well-being for you everywhere, and may no evil come upon them.
May all beings, all living creatures, and all elements without exception—may they all indeed possess the crest-lock of enlightenment; may they all be free from affliction.
May all behold auspicious things; may no one encounter evil. Whatever beings have gathered here, whether standing upon the earth or in the atmosphere—
May they always practice loving-kindness toward all beings,
and may they practice the Dharma by day and by night.
Oṃ vajrapuṣpe svāhā. Offering of food: Oṃ vajranaivedya svāhā.
Oṃ! O Lord, please accept at your pleasure this conduct of the Vajra-samaya, consisting of food to be chewed and eaten and so forth, endowed with excellent color, fragrance, and taste.
Now, the libation (tarpaṇa):
Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, the Hero, Lord of Heroes, huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, salutation to him who resembles the fire at the end of a great aeon, huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to the one with a fierce crown of matted hair! Huṃ huṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, homage to the one with a face terrifyingly fierce like a gaping maw! Huṃ huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to the one radiant with a thousand arms! Huṃ huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to the one who bears the axe, the noose, the trident, and the khaṭvāṅga; huṃ huṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to the one who wears a tiger-skin garment; huṃ huṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, homage to the one whose body is like great smoky darkness; huṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā!
The offering of divine milk:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-cintāmṛta-dhāre svāhā.
The offering of the lamp.
Delightful to the eyes, containing many treasuries of jewels, with lotus-feet honored by lords of men,
and with the net of delusion destroyed by the lamp of wisdom— those who there worship the rows of lamps [attain such a state].

Oṃ vajradīpe hrīṃ svāhā. Then, having consecrated parched grain one hundred and eight times with the root mantra and reciting the verse beginning with "ye dharmā," one should scatter it before the deity. Having offered the bali offering with the verse beginning with "akāramukha," and so forth.
Having offered the sacrificial fee with the words beginning "O Mañjuśrī," one should recite the hundred-syllable dhāraṇī with hands joined in añjali and holding unbroken grains (*akṣata*).
Then, having made a mandala with water for the purpose of offering the *akṣatas*, one should scatter ten flowers there with these mantras:
*oṃ pīṭhāya svāhā*.
Oṃ, to the secondary seat, svāhā! Oṃ, to the field, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the secondary field, svāhā!
Oṃ, to Chandā, svāhā! Oṃ, to Upachandā, svāhā! Oṃ, to Melāpaka, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the secondary gathering place, svāhā!
Oṃ, to the cremation ground, svāhā! Oṃ, to the secondary cremation ground, svāhā!
There, having performed the worship with the five offerings, one should present the bali.

Oṃ! To all the heroes and heroines dwelling in the seats, sub-seats, fields, sub-fields, chandas, sub-chandas, meeting places, sub-meeting places, cremation grounds, and sub-cremation grounds, I bow with devotion.
Then, at the time of offering the unhusked rice (*akṣata*), one should recite the hymns to be described hereafter:
Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ.
"O Śrī Vajrasattva and so forth!
To you, O Śrī Saṃvara, who are the mass of the wisdom of the omniscient one, who accomplishes the welfare of the world, and who have arisen like a wish-fulfilling gem— homage be to you!"
O Śrī Saṃvara, homage be to you, who are the great primordial wisdom pervading the universe, eternally abiding within the self of all, and who are the great fierce one of compassion and wrath!
Having recited these and other verses, one should perform the offering of forgiveness (*kṣamārpaṇa*).
Regarding that offering of forgiveness:

after the recitation of the hundred-syllable mantra, and immediately following the statement of the mental resolve for what is desired by the donor and others—beginning with the words "O donors" and so forth—one should perform the offering of forgiveness in this manner.
O Lord, because I have not attained [perfection], my wisdom is incapable;
O Protector, you should forgive all that which is deficient or excessive.

May the perfectly awakened Buddhas, the deities, and those who observe their vows; Brahmā and the other world-protectors, as well as all beings engaged in ritual activities, please grant me forgiveness.
For the sake of bestowing grace upon my devotee, grant peace, well-being, and prosperity;
as for whatever evil deed has been committed by me once again through my deluded intellect.
And you, O Protector, must forgive [us], if you are the savior of embodied beings;
O Lord of Generosity, always grant peace, well-being, and prosperity.
Whatever evil has been committed born of the body, whatever evil has been committed born of speech,
and whatever evil has been committed born of the mind— all that I confess.
Homage be to you, O Buddha of infinite range; homage be to you, O Sage who reveals the truth.
May I and all beings be established in the truth, and may all our endeavors bear fruit.

"O Supreme Lord, O Supreme Goddess, be gracious! Protect me! Forgive my ten million transgressions—whatever is deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, or deficient in the words of meditation.
Having thus sought forgiveness, one should dismiss the invited deities.
Having granted you the accomplishment of the welfare of all sentient beings according to your needs,
go now to the realm of the Buddhas, and return once more.
Go each to your own place!
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ vajramaṇḍalam mūri— this is the dismissal.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the daily worship;
may there be the accomplishment of the welfare of all sentient beings.
